paraphrase: In the Kula scripture certain substances ordinarily held impure — bodily fluids and the products of the cow among them — are declared purifiers for the daily and occasional rites, to be used without doubt or hesitation.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage. Restricted content: summary only, no method, per the project rules.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: Oneself is the guru, oneself the siddha, oneself the disciple, oneself Śiva; bondage is from ignorance, knowledge is release. The partless one takes fragrance and stench alike and is unstained, like a lotus leaf in water; so the yogī is not stained by merit or sin — neither the sin of killing a brahmin nor the fruit of the horse sacrifice, neither bathing at all fords nor the touch of foreigners seizes him.

original.text: स्वयं गुरुः स्वयं सिद्धः स्वयं शिष्यः स्वयं शिवः । अज्ञानबन्धनाज्ञेयं ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं विमोचनम् सुगन्धं पूतिगन्धञ्च नित्यं गृह्णाति निष्कलः । पद्मपत्रे यथा तोये तथा चैवं न लिप्यते तद्वन्न लिप्यते योगी पुण्यपापैः सुरेश्वरि । ब्रह्महत्यादिकं पापम् अश्वमेधादिकं फलम् सर्वतीर्थाभिषेकञ्च म्लेच्छादिस्पर्शनेन तु । एतैर्न गृह्यते योगी क्रियमाणैरपि स्फुटम्
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: Success is born for one ever joined in non-duality (advaita); one who makes duality is carried off by the yoginīs; one fallen from the pledge (samaya) is an 'animal'. Abandoning the attitude of duality, one should be formed by non-dual conduct (advaitācāra).

original.text: अद्वैते नित्ययुक्तस्य तस्य सिद्धिः प्रजायते । द्वैतन्तु कारयेद्यस्तु आकृष्टो योगिभिस्तु सः समयाद् भ्रष्टन्तु यो देवि स पशुर्नात्र संशयः । द्वैतभावं परित्यज्य अद्वैताचारभावितः
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: Evenness, freedom from passion, indifference, living like the sky, non-possession and contentment; he should not practise the yoga of the pairs, and should give up desire, anger, pride and greed little by little; he should not despise the caru or the non-dual pledge.

original.text: समत्वं वीतरागत्वमुदासीनां ख-वृत्तिनाम् । निष्परिग्रहसन्तोषं द्वन्द्वयोगं न कारयेत् कामक्रोधञ्च दम्भञ्च त्यजेल्लोभं शनैः शनैः । न चरुन्निन्दयेद्भद्रे समयाद्वैतमेव च
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The conduct of the non-dual caru is to be practised as governed by the power of will: without the person's will one must not do that caru by force.

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: Of vessels — clay, turtle-shell, bronze, copper, gold, silver, shell, glass, horn, wood, stone — the skull (kapāla) is the best of all; lacking it, a large coconut shell may serve.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage. 12.13 names 'viśvāmitra-kapāla' (reading uncertain).
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The forms of conduct (caryā): as a child, as a madman, as a king, as one filthy, as the independent one, as hero-leader, as gandharva, naked, as triple-staff bearer and others — whatever wish he forms, that is his vow. He should worship his own guru daily at the three times and offer himself to the guru in mind, deed and speech, devoted to guru and Kaula scripture and formed by non-dual conduct.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: Liberation confirmed by experience: one should say 'haṃsa haṃsa' always in the body; by that which pervades the three worlds all-knowing arises; the mind is not to be grasped, nor concentration held — one whose mind is beyond mind (unmana) is liberated here; one who sees a throbbing garland of jewels at the end of the twelve (dvādaśānta) is liberated and unstained by sin and merit, like a drop on a lotus leaf.

original.text: हंस हंस वदेन्नित्यं देहस्थावरजङ्गमे । श्रुत्वा तस्य पतिर्दिव्यं याति मोक्षवरं शुभम् येन व्याप्तं च त्रैलोक्यं जगद् यस्मिन् व्यवस्थितम् । तं ज्ञात्वा गूढसद्भावं सर्वज्ञत्वम्प्रजायते न तेन विना मुच्यन्ते व्यवहारान्न हि तद्विना । शुभाशुभं च सम्भोक्तं न तेन रहितं क्वचित् न मनञ्चित्तमालब्धं न पेयं धारणं प्रिये । उन्मनन्तु मनो यस्य तस्य मोक्षो भवन्तीह द्वादशान्ते यदा पश्येत् स्फूरन्तं मणिमालिका । तस्य मोक्षो भवेद्यस्तु पापपुण्यैर्न लिप्यते देवयाने महायाने यस्य चित्तं सदा प्रिये । तस्य मोक्षो न सन्देहः पद्मपत्राम्बुबिन्दुवत्
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: By the placing (nyāsa) of syllables on the body in this order, liberation preceded by the highest awareness is certain; at the fall of the body the skull splits.

original.text: सः रूं वक्त्रम् ॥ सः यं नाभि ॥ सः षु। मेढ्रः ॥ सः लं गुदे ॥ इदं न्यासक्रमन्देवि यस्य देहे प्रवर्तते । तस्य मोक्षो न सन्देहः परं संवित्तिपूर्वकम् ॥ पिण्डपाते यदा देवि कपालम्भिद्यते तदा
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The Goddess asks for the means free from nets of mantra, from breath-control and from meditation on the centres, that gives success at once.

original.text: मन्त्रजालविनिर्मुक्तम्प्राणायामविवर्जितम् । चक्रध्यानविनिर्मुक्तं सद्यः सिद्धिकरं परम्
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027

speaker: the Goddess (Devī)

paraphrase: This is the supreme by which all that moves and stands was created and into which it dissolves, as a river into the ocean; by being firmly established in it one is not stained by merit or sin.

original.text: एतन्ते परमं देवि येन सृष्टं चराचरः । अस्मिन्नेव लयं भद्रे समुद्रेण नदी यथा अनेन दृढमात्रेण पुण्यपापैर्न लिप्यते । पिण्डमष्टप्रकारेण अष्टधातुपदं प्रिये
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027

notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from the verse(s).
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: When one practises on the root centre (mūlacakra) wonders arise: first trembling, then shaking, trembling of hands, feet and head, speech in many tongues, spontaneous mantras and seals, hopping like a frog, leaving the ground, poetry, knowledge of past and future, cheating of time, change of form, the end of wrinkles and grey hair, movement in the sky and the eight powers — this is the root Kaula.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: Fixing the mind in the heart and remaining absorbed in it, one enters samādhi with the marks of seizure and possession: the limbs revolve, cries arise, the city is stirred; with practice come knowledge of past and future, hearing from afar, entering others' bodies, destruction of death and meeting with the yoginīs.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: This Kaula is not to be given to one without devotion to the Kula or the guru, nor to disciples slightly tested — the deceitful, the miserly, the deluded, those who revile truth or hate gods, fire and ascetics; the teacher who gives to such loses his power. He should choose a disciple who obeys the guru, examines what is fit, delights in dharma, is free of anger, resolute, desireless, discreet, living alone, of clear mind and firm devotion, and test him well; never to the lustful, the angry, the one who reviles Śiva or the Kula-Bhairava.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: One should think of neither water nor fire, air nor space, neither below, above nor middle, like wood or a clod; when the mind comes to the mind-less state (unmanībhāva), making the mind void of void, free of thought and motionless, the jīva dissolved in that is not roused even when beaten with drums, conches, tabors, lutes and flutes; he becomes undecaying and deathless.

original.text: अतोर्द्धं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणु त्वं वीरवन्दिते । न जलं चिन्तयेद्देवि न वह्निवायुराकाशम् नाधस्तादूर्द्धमध्यञ्च काष्ठवल्लोष्ट्रवत् प्रिये । मनस्य उन्मनीभावो यदा भवति सुन्दरि शून्यशून्यमनः कृत्वा निश्चिन्तो निश्चलस्थितिः । घटपटस्थितस्तम्भा ग्रामकूपादिकं बुधः भेरिशङ्खमृदङ्गैश्च वीणावंशनिनादितैः । ताड्यमानन्नबोध्यते जीवस्तल्लयतां गतः भूतं भव्यं भविष्यञ्च अतीतानागतन्तथा । अक्षयो ह्यमरो भूत्वा कामदेवद्वितीयकः
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027
original.licence: e-text quoted with attribution; licence as for the source file

notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from the verse(s).
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: Without nectar how can there be immortality? The nectar is the true Kaula nature, of the nature of kāmakalā: the principle abiding within the innate (sahaja), throbbing, pure as a jewel, like a pearl or a firefly, sparkling like the stars in the sky, white, red, black, smoky and yellow — the maker of creation and dissolution, beyond Akula and Kula.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: Free of wrinkles, grey hair, fever and disease, undecaying, deathless and eternal, when dissolution comes he sees all that moves and stands and remains with Bhairava, creator and destroyer like him; with even mind always absorbed in the bone-circle the body stands like a thunderbolt and there is no dissolution for it — 'I practised this before, and so I am imperishable.'
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: Asked how he preserved himself when all perished in the single ocean, Bhairava reveals the innate centre (sahaja-cakra) in the bone-circle: by the practice of the vajra-yoga a man becomes like a thunderbolt (vajra).
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: 'I am that supreme principle, I am Bhairava, Sadāśiva, Īśa, Śrīkaṇṭha and Rudra; I am that fisherman (dhīvara), I am the lord of heroes; I am Ananta, Rudra, destruction itself.' He explains the names of the Kaula gurus as his own: Viśvapāda because the universe came forth from him, Vicitra from the variegated creation, Śvetapāda, Bhṛṅgapāda, Bhaṭṭapāda as lord of gods and demons, Śrīkaṇṭha, Rurupāda, Śrīnātha.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: When Bhairava and the Goddess went to Candradvīpa, Kārttikeya came in the form of the boy Baṭuka and in ignorance stole the scripture; as a mouse he cast it into the sea, where a great fish swallowed it. Bhairava, casting a net of power (śakti-jāla), became a fisherman (kaivarta), drew out the fish, split its belly and recovered the Kaula scripture — 'I am that fisherman'; hence the brahmin became a fisherman and 'fish-killer' (Matsyaghna).
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage. The fisherman-Bhairava is the ground of Matsyendra's names Macchaghna/Mīnanātha.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The Kaula was brought down according to the four ages: in the first as Jñānanirṇiti, in the second called Mahat, in the third named Siddhāmṛta, and in the Kali age as Matsyodara ('from the fish's belly'); from the Mahākaula came the Siddhakaula.

original.text: महाकौलात् सिद्धकौलं सिद्धकौलात् मसादरम् (?) । चतुर्युगविभागेन अवतारञ्चोदितं मया ज्ञानदौ निर्णीतिः कौलं द्वितीये महत् सञ्ज्ञितम् । तृतीये सिद्धामृतन्नाम कलौ मत्स्योदरं प्रिये
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: Bhairava is present at Śrīśaila, Mahendra and the famed seat Kāmākhyā, where siddhas meet at the three times; those whose minds are fixed on the meditation of space see him there with the Goddess; at Kāmākhyā meeting the yoginīs one becomes equal to them and gains whatever form is thought and the eight powers.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: In the Siddhāmṛta it is said that blaming the guru is condemned: through such a lapse the scripture fell into the ocean; in the dreadful Kali age, though accomplished by divine ones, he received his curse as told in every tantra.

original.text: सिद्धामृते तु यत् प्रोक्तं गुरोर्निन्दा विगर्हिता । तथ्याच्यवनसञ्जातं पतितं च महोदधौ कलौ युगे महाघोरे दिव्यैः संसाधितोऽपि सः । तन्त्रे तन्त्रे समाख्यातं यथाशापन्तु प्राप्तवान्
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027

notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from the verse(s).
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: Knowing the gross, subtle and supreme haṃsa as all, the Kaula doctrine passes by succession from ear to ear; it is not to be given to the untested but to the well-tested; after the Kula consecration (abhiṣeka) the teaching on the self is to be revealed.

original.text: स्थूलं सूक्ष्मं परो हंसौ ज्ञात्वा सर्वात्मकं प्रिये । पारम्पर्यान् मतं कौलं कर्णात् कर्णगतं परम् अपरीक्ष्ये न दातव्यं दातव्यं सुपरीक्षिते । कृत्वा कुलाभिषेकन्तु प्रकाश्यं त्वात्मनिर्णयम्
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027
original.licence: e-text quoted with attribution; licence as for the source file

notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from the verse(s).
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: Five jewels are to be known in the Kula scripture: first the arresting of grey hair, second the attainment of what is desired, third taking forms at will, fourth the imperishable portion, fifth the great jewel, destruction of old age and death.

original.text: पञ्चरत्नादि देवेशि ज्ञातव्या तु कुलागमे । प्रथमं पलितस्तम्भं द्वितीयम् ईप्सितं भवेत् तृतीयं कामरूपत्वं चतुर्थमक्षयांशकम् । पञ्चमन्तु महारत्नं जरामरणनाशनम्
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027
original.licence: e-text quoted with attribution; licence as for the source file

notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from the verse(s).
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: In the great pervasion (mahāvyāpti), the great sleep, the knower of the principle neither hears nor sees nor knows smell — fragrant or foul, camphor or sandal; in it is knowledge of past and future and the cheating of time.

original.text: महाव्याप्तिमहानिद्रां न शृणोति न पश्यति । सुगन्धं पूतिगन्धं वा कर्पूरञ्चन्दनादिषु न गन्धं वेत्ति तत्त्वज्ञो महाव्याप्तिरियं प्रिये । अतीतानागतञ्चैव तस्मिन् कालस्य वञ्चनम्
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027
original.licence: e-text quoted with attribution; licence as for the source file

notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from the verse(s).
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The haṃsa plays below and above and dissolves again at the end of the twelve; still in the heart like water in a pot, fine as a lotus fibre, beyond being and non-being, beyond support and supported, all-knowing, risen everywhere, it moves up and down by itself: the innate principle (sahaja-tattva) delights in others as in oneself. The sound in the throat is the divine, higher-and-lower; the coiled Vāmā from the soles to the crown rises from the anus and dissolves at the end of the twelve; so the haṃsa moves in the body, stainless, partless, pure, eternal bliss, with out-breath and in-breath.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The knowledge within the body is of eleven kinds — the secret place, the navel, the downward-facing lotus of the heart, the centre that stops the breath, the cool knot of the uvula, the tip of the nose, the end of the twelve, the point between the brows, the forehead, the brahmarandhra and the radiant summit; men suffer greatly not knowing the Kula scripture; the innate one (sahaja) abiding in the heart is to be remembered.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: He is the self and doer; the body alone has pain, joy and sorrow, old age and death, hunger, thirst, delusion, fear and greed; he is not cut by weapons, nor burnt by fire, nor drowned by water. By the jīva the world is created: the jīva is lord of the principles, the person, the haṃsa, the all-pervading supreme Śiva. The self is the first guru: the self binds itself and the self releases itself, lord of itself; knowing the self by the self, one is king of yogīs.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: He is called Śiva himself; liberated, he liberates others, ever pure like a lotus in mud; taking a human body, that Śiva plays on earth. By his mere touch there is liberation; by receiving his leavings, by being bathed or anointed by him, by the touch of his foot one becomes fit for liberation; when he eats, all that moves and stands has eaten.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage. In the e-text vv. 38–39 are misnumbered 78–79.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: Without Śiva there is no Śakti, nor is Śiva without Śakti; they go on together like fire and smoke; there is no shade without a tree nor tree without shade; the yogī devoted to the practice of Śakti attains sameness in the Kula.

original.text: न शिवेन विना शक्तिर्न शक्तिरहितः शिवः । अन्योऽन्यञ्च प्रवर्तन्ते अग्निधूमौ यथा प्रिये न वृक्षरहिता च्छाया न छायारहितो द्रुमः । शक्त्याभ्यासरतो योगी कुले सामान्यतां व्रजेत्
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The seven nether worlds and the heavens above them — the fourteen worlds — are to be known as situated within the body in the form of principles (tattvas); all dissolves in the domain of Śakti.

original.text: सप्तपातालमुद्दिष्टं तस्योर्द्धे स्वर्गसंस्थितम् । एतानि कथिता भद्रे भुवनानि चतुर्दश ज्ञातव्या देहमध्ये तु तत्त्वरूपा स्थिता प्रिये । सर्वज्ञा (यत्न ?) संलीनं लयञ्च शक्तिगोचरे
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: In dissolution Śakti goes into Śiva, and Śiva abides within action; action is absorbed in knowledge and dissolves through will; the power of will goes to dissolution where the supreme Śiva is the light. So dissolution is told by its stages.

original.text: शिवमध्ये गता शक्तिः क्रियामध्यस्थितः शिवः । ज्ञानमध्ये क्रिया लीना क्रिया लीयति इच्छया इच्छाशक्तिर्लयं याति यत्र तेजः परः शिवः । संहारन्तु इमं भेदेन कथितन्तव शोभने
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: Enjoyment (bhukti) is situated below and liberation (mukti) above; by the method of creation and dissolution the foundation of the Kula (kulādhāra) has been described.

original.text: अधस्था संस्थिता भुक्तिः ऊर्द्धं मुक्तिर्वरानने । पूर्वं यत् सूचितं देवि सृष्टियोगं मया तव
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: A proof of liberation: by a forceful upward practice with the breath, the skull splits and the jīva goes to the spotless; becoming the all-pervading Śiva, creator and destroyer, he knows himself as supreme and knows all; for him there is no sorrow, only continuous joy.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage. Restricted content: summary only, no method, per the project rules. A forced departure from the body; no method reproduced.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The beginningless and endless Śakti named Will, born of Śiva, is called Vyomamālinī and Khecarī, Vāmā, Kuṇḍalī, Jyeṣṭhā and Manonmanī, the famed power of Rudra, sung as Kāmākhyā; foremost of all, she is neither written nor read, and is praised in all books as Mātṛkā, the mass of sounds.

original.text: अनादिनिधना शक्तिरिच्छा नाम शिवोद्भवा । व्योममालिनी सा भद्रे खेचरीति निगद्यते वामाख्या कुण्डलीनाम ज्येष्ठा चैव मनोन्मनी । रुद्रशक्तिस्तु विख्याता कामाख्या तु गीयते अग्रणी चैव सर्वेषां लिख्यते न च पठ्यते । मातृका शब्दरा(शिश्च) सर्वग्रन्थेषु कीर्त्यते
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The marks of the Śakti and the hero (vīra): she is devoted to the Kula and worships guru and Goddess, fearless, of good conduct and rare; the hero is of good nature, truthful, resolute, devoted to guru and Kaula scripture, free of anger, brave, confident through his own body, knowing the Śakti born of the body, endowed with knowledge and formed by non-dual conduct.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: No lunar day, no constellation, no fast is prescribed: wherever the yogī abides he should rely on knowledge alone.

original.text: न तिथिर्न च नक्षत्रं नोपवासं विधीयते । यत्र तत्र स्थितो योगी ज्ञानमेवं समाश्रयेत् । कथितं कौलसद्भावं नाम्ना ज्ञानस्य निर्णये
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027

notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from the verse(s).
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The Kaula scriptures and their branches are named: the Kulapañcāśikā, Kulasāgara, Kulogha, Hṛdaya, Bhairavodyānaka, Candrakaula and the Jñānanirṇaya; from these came the Sṛṣṭikaula, Mahākaula, Timira, Siddhāmṛta, Mātakaula, Śaktibheda, Ūrmikaula, Siddheśvara and the Vajra-born Kaula — the union of the Jñāna-kaula in the four ages.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage. Several names are uncertain readings in the e-text.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: This essence, drawn out of the Jñānanirṇaya of vast extent, is in Kāmarūpa in every house of the yoginīs; by its grace they work restraint and grace and the meeting of siddhas; the great scripture came down from Candradvīpa and is sung at Kāmākhyā as 'abiding in the great fish's belly'.

original.text: तस्य मध्ये इमं नाथ सारभूतं समुद्धृतम् । कामरूपे इमं शास्त्रं योगिनीनां गृहे गृहे निग्रहानुग्रहञ्चैव सिद्धिमेलापकं तथा । कुर्वन्ति सततं देवि अस्य ज्ञानप्रसादतः चन्द्रद्वीपं महाशास्त्रम् अवतीर्णं सुलोचने । कामाख्ये गीयते नाथे महामत्स्योदरस्थितिः
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027

speaker: the Goddess (Devī)

paraphrase: What was hidden is now revealed, to be proclaimed on earth in the Kula scripture; the lineage of the siddhas is to be made known; the adept keeps his mark hidden (gupta-liṅgī), is devoted to guru-worship, affectionate to all people and compassionate to all beings.

original.text: यत् पुरा गोपितं भद्रे तत् सर्वं प्रकटीकृतः । भूलोके देवतानाञ्च कथितव्यं कुलागमे सिद्धानाञ्च विशेषेण ख्यापनीयं कुलान्व(यम्) । समयाचारसमोपेतं विज्ञानं द्वैतवासिनाम् गुप्तलिङ्गी सदा कालं गुरुपूजनतत्परः । वत्सलः सर्वलोकानां सर्वजीवदयान्वितः
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: One must never be angry with a girl or a woman who speaks; women under a vow and maidens are to be honoured with effort by those in the Kula; meditating on the heroine within oneself, adorned with jewels, one should give up external worship — this worship gives enjoyment and liberation.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The yoginīs move on earth in the forms of the pigeon, vulture, swan, hen, owl, jackal, goat, buffalo, cat, tiger, elephant, peacock and other creatures; appearing in fearful forms they quickly seize the 'animal'.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: That liṅga is not of wood, clay, stone, jewel or metal; what is worshipped by the eighteen worldly teachings should not be worshipped even in the mind, for those who worship so are 'animals' (paśu) without knowledge, outside the Kula command; one should not keep company with them.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The Kula aim: where the gaze is, there is the mind. Place, meditation, letter and aim are four: the place is called the body (piṇḍa), meditation the state (pada), the letter is form (rūpa), and the aim is beyond form (rūpātīta); each of these is fourfold in every place.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The Kaulika who desires success should worship this liṅga with mental flowers: the first flower is non-harming, the second restraint of the senses, the third compassion, the fourth feeling (bhāva), the fifth patience, the sixth conquest of anger, the seventh meditation, the eighth knowledge. Knowing this rule and worshipping the liṅga in the body, one gains enjoyment and liberation; this liṅga of success abiding in the body is the mark of the Kaula body-liṅga.

original.text: एतन्तु पूजयेद्देवि कौलिकं सिद्धिमिच्छता । अर्चयेन्मानसैः पुष्पैः सुगन्धैर्धूपदीपितैः अहिंसा प्रथमं पुष्पं द्वितीयेन्द्रियनि(ग्र)हम् । तृतीयन्तु दयापुष्पम्भावपुष्पञ्चतुर्थकम् पञ्चमन्तु क्षमापुष्पं षष्ठं क्रोधविनिर्जितम् । सप्तमं ध्यानपुष्पन्तु ज्ञानपुष्पन्तु अष्टमम् एतत् पुष्पविधिं ज्ञात्वा अर्चयेल्लिङ्गमानसम् । भुक्तिमुक्तिमवाप्नोति देहलिङ्गार्चनेन तु सिद्धिलिङ्गमिदं देवि देहस्थं प्रत्ययान्वितम् । मनोलिङ्गं सदा ध्यायेद् यां यां फलसमीकृते तां लभन्ते न सन्देहो आत्मसम्बित्तिपूर्वकम् । एतत् ते कौलिकन्देवि देहलिङ्गस्य लक्षणम्
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027
original.licence: e-text quoted with attribution; licence as for the source file

notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from the verse(s).
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: Other liṅgas of stone, wood or clay are to be abandoned: the worldly path lacks success and liberation. One whose tendency (vāsanā) rests in the body has a share in the Kula teaching; one whose tendency is outside is an 'animal' coloured by externals.

original.text: अन्यन्तु वर्जयेद्देवि पाषाणं काष्ठमृन्मयम् । लौकिकम् मार्गसम्पन्ना सिद्धिमुक्तिविवर्जिता देहस्था वासना यस्य तस्यैवांशो कुलागमे । बहिस्था वासना यस्य सः पशुरङ्गरञ्जितः
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027
original.licence: e-text quoted with attribution; licence as for the source file

notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from the verse(s).
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: Above the thousand-petalled and ten-million-petalled lotuses is the all-pervading, ever-risen, undivided, independent and spotless one; by its will creation arises and in it dissolution occurs — hence it is called the liṅga in which all that moves and stands dissolves. Not knowing it is bondage, knowing it one is released. It is beyond mind (unmana), free from meditation and concentration, always directly present, made of all letters yet devoid of letters, reached by knowledge and handed down in succession.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: This most secret cause of success is to be guarded with effort from the wicked and those without devotion; it is not to be given to one lacking devotion by those who desire Kaula success.

original.text: सर्वज्ञगुणसम्पूर्ण इत्येवं भैरवोऽब्रवीत् । यत् त्वयापृच्छितम्भद्रे सुगोप्य सिद्धिकारणम् गोपितव्यम्प्रयत्नेन दुष्टानाम्भक्तिवर्जितम् । न देयं भक्तिहीनस्य कौलिकीं सिद्धिमिच्छताम्
original.edition: Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The centres are in the genitals, navel, heart, throat, mouth, head, the top of the crown-lock, the junction of the skull and, in the middle of the back, the triple staff: the centres are of eleven kinds, with the thousand-petalled; their petals number five, eight, ten, twelve, sixteen, a hundred and ten million.

original.text: पूज्यते सुरवृन्दैस्तु दिव्यकन्यारनेकधा । गुह्यनाभिहृदि कण्ठे वक्त्रे मूर्ध्नि शिखान्तरे मुण्डसन्धिगता देवि पृष्ठमध्ये त्रिदण्डकम् । एकादशविधा देवि चक्राणि च सहस्रिका पञ्चारम् अष्टपत्रञ्च दश द्वादश पत्रकम् । षोडशं शतपत्रञ्च कोटिपत्रं यथैव च

paraphrase: Meditating separately on bindu, nāda and Śakti, one attains dharma, wealth, desire and liberation, the eight powers beginning with minuteness, knowledge of past and future and change of form. Through devotion to the guru and to the yoginīs in the Kula and Kaula scriptures there is immortality (amaratva); one conquers death, without doubt.

original.text: बिन्दुनादतथाशक्तिरेवं ध्यात्वा पृथक् पृथक् । धर्मार्थौ काममोक्षौ च अणिमादिगुणाष्टकम् अतीतानागतन्देवि रूपस्य परिवर्तनम् । भवत्येवं न सन्देहो अभ्यासात् तद्गतस्य तु गुरुभक्तिर्योगिनीनां कुलकौलागमेषु च । अमरत्वं भवेद्देवि जयेन्मृत्युं न संशयः

paraphrase: The conquest of death, the settled knowledge of all, is to be kept secret with effort in the world of mortals from base men; this rare heap of powers is to be given only to one already accomplished and tested for a year.

original.text: कथितं मृत्युञ्जयन्देवि सर्वज्ञानस्य निर्णयम् । गोपितव्यं प्रयत्नेन मर्त्यलोके नराधमे दुर्लभं सिद्धिसन्दोहं गोपितव्यं प्रयत्नतः । दातव्यं पूर्वसिद्धस्य अब्दमेकपरीक्षितम्

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The conquest of death: one who contemplates the white, cool, fragrant, radiant nectar that gladdens like the moon, coming from the middle of the sky and flowing through the many openings, soon conquers death; for him there is no old age, death or disease. The wise one should contemplate himself seated on a vast white lotus in the ocean of milk, covered above by a like lotus and sprinkled with its drops; he is freed from diseases and the bonds of old age and death and takes whatever form he wishes.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: This essence of the Kaula, born of the yoginīs, is to be given to one devoted to the Kula scripture, who worships guru and Goddess, is endowed with every good disposition and firm in resolve — not to the deceitful, the crooked, the cruel, or those who bear sectarian marks with display.

original.text: कुलागमसुभक्ताय गुरुदेव्या प्रपूजके । सर्वभावोपपन्नस्य दातव्यं कृतनिश्चये मायाविने शठे क्रूरे प्रपञ्चैर्लिङ्गिने तथा । न देयं कौलिकं सारं योगिनीनान्तु सम्भवम्

paraphrase: Placing the mind in the heart until it reaches the mind-less state (unmanatā), one destroys a death that has already come within half a ghaṭikā: this is the cheating of time, the most secret made manifest.

original.text: न मृत्युर्भवते तस्य अब्दात् स्वच्छन्दगो भवेत् । हृदिस्थञ्च मनः कृत्वा यावदुन्मनतां गतः आगतं नाशयेन्मृत्युं घटिकार्द्धे वरानने । कालस्य वञ्चनं देवि सुगोप्यं प्रकटीकृतम्

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The jīva is the supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease and spotless; it is called the lord (nātha), the all-pervading supreme Śiva; that jīva is the haṃsa, the 'person' of Śakti; it is mind, breath, intellect and thought, the air that fills all beings. As long as it abides in the body it is called jīva; as soon as the body is left it is called the supreme Śiva.

original.text: शृणु त्वं वीरचामुण्डे वरं जीवस्य निर्णयम् । स(ः)परं निष्कलं नित्यं निरामयनिरञ्जनम् परमाणुमुच्यते नाथो स शिवो व्यापकः परः । स(ः) जीवः परतरो यस्तु स(ः) हंसः शक्तिपुद्गल(ः) स(ः) मनो मत्परं प्राणः स(ः) बुद्धिश्चित्तमेव च । समीरपूरको वायुः सर्वजीवेषु संस्थितम्(ः) देहस्थस्तिष्ठते यावत्तावज्जीवोऽपि गीयते । स देहत्यक्तमात्रेण परं शिवो निगद्यते

paraphrase: The (living) sound heard in navel, heart, throat, mouth, nostrils and ear comes down in succession from teacher to teacher; this Kaula teaching has come from ear to ear. It is to be given to one devoted to the Kula scriptures who worships guru and Goddess and is firmly resolved, never to the deceitful, the crooked, the cruel or the false ascetic.

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: It dwells in the navel, heart, throat, mouth, nostrils and ears; this Kaula teaching is heard as handed down in succession, passed from ear to ear; by merely knowing and hearing it one is freed of all sins.

original.text: नाभिस्थं हृदि कण्ठे च वक्त्रनासापुटन्तथा । कर्णस्थं श्रूयते देवि पारम्पर्यक्रमागतम् कौलिकन्तु इदं देवि कर्णात् कर्णसमागतम् । अनेन ज्ञानमात्रेण श्रुतेन च वरानने

paraphrase: From steady practice of these meditations successive attainments arise: first people's affection, second the destruction of disease, third graceful poetry, fourth mastery of speech, fifth hearing from afar, sixth leaving the ground, seventh meeting with the yoginīs, eighth the removal of old age, ninth fierce speed, tenth taking many forms; the eleventh is peace, beyond the three kinds — endowed with eleven qualities he is worshipped like Śiva.

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: Once the Kaula is known, restraint of the mind (mano-rodha) is not to be done: the scripture is free of elaboration (prapañca), the guru is free of it, the mantra is free of it, Śiva is free of it — this is the Kaula scripture; those caught in elaboration are 'animals'.

original.text: मनोरोधं न कर्तव्यं यदा ज्ञातं हि कौलिकम् । प्रपञ्चरहितं शास्त्रं प्रपञ्चरहितो गुरुः प्रपञ्चरहितो मन्त्रः प्रपञ्चरहितः शिवः । एतत् कौलागमं नाथ अप्रपञ्चैः पशुः प्रिये

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The Śaktis born of sacred fields are worshipped at Karavīra, Mahākāla, Devīkoṭa, Vārāṇasī, Prayāga, Caritra, Ekāmraka, Aṭṭahāsa and Jayantī; of the seats (pīṭha) the first is Kāmākhyā with seven sub-seats, the second Pūrṇagiri, then the great seat Oḍiyāna and Arbuda — seats and sub-seats, fields and sub-fields.

speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The eight-by-eight (aṣṭāṣṭaka) of the sixty-four yoginīs is taught with its circles (cakras); worship and meditation of each great circle brings a power — the eight qualities, attraction, entering another's body, knowledge of past and future, speech in unheard tongues, liberation — 'knowing the eight-by-eight rule one succeeds, not otherwise'.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: Kaula worship is performed in a solitary place with garlands, incense, food, fish, meat and wine, joined with a Śakti; the outer Śaktis are of three kinds, and the inner (ādhyātmika) Śakti, which produces the bliss of desire within the body, is the innate (sahajā) one; three are in the body and three outside.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage. Restricted content: summary only, no method, per the project rules.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The guru-lineage of the Kaula is worshipped by name — Viśvapāda, Vicitrapāda, Śvetapāda, Bhaṭṭapāda, Macchendrapāda and others — with the yoginīs; in the dreadful Kali age sixteen siddhas arose in this Kaula, and the former great siddhas (Mṛṣṇipāda, Avatārapāda, Sūryapāda and others) brought down the Kula and Kaula in the four ages.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Kaulajñānanirṇaya, ed. P. C. Bagchi, Calcutta Sanskrit Series 3 (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00027); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: In each of the four ages Siddhas brought down the Kula; the text names the great Siddhas of this Kaula (e.g. Vyāghrapāda, Pañcaśikhipāda, Lambodarapāda); the Mahākaula passed by the will of the supreme from Icchā yoginī to the sky-going (khecarī) yoginīs, from them to the Mothers and to the earth-going (bhūcarī) yoginīs; one born in the family of the yoginīs obtains the Kaula clearly and becomes dear to the yoginīs, gaining enjoyment, liberation and great perfection.
